Bengaluru (in short 'the Tribunal').

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 29.06.2013 at about 10:30 A.M., husband of petitioner No.1, father of petitioner No.4 and son of petitioners No.2 and 3 by name Kanagaraj.S, the deceased, while riding his Bike bearing Registration No.KA-50-Q-6676 near Allalsandra Railway Gate, Yelahanka Main Road, a KSRTC Bus bearing Registration No.KA-40-F-310 hit against him due to which he sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to death during transit to the hospital.

Petitioners being the dependents approached the Tribunal for NC: 2024:KHC:32341 grant of compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- against the KSRTC and owner and insurer of the Honda Activa bearing Registration No.KA-03-HF-9043.
The claim was opposed by the respondents.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.15,02,600/- with interest @ 8% p.a.
fastening the liability equally against the KSRTC as well as insurer & owner of the Honda Activa.

Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioners have filed MFA No.2067/2015, whereas questioning the liability fastened, the Insurer of the Bike has filed MFA No.2336/2015.

Heard the argument of Shri M.H.Prakash, learned counsel for the petitioners, Shri O.Mahesh,
learned counsel for the Insurer of the Bike and Shri D.Vijayakumar, learned counsel for the KSRTC.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for petitioners that the deceased, apart from working as a Sale Executive in Dr.Agarwal's Health Care Ltd., was also doing transport business and earning additional income apart from his salary.
At the time of the accident, his salary was Rs.10,500/- per month apart from his business income.

The Income Tax NC: 2024:KHC:32341 Returns have been placed before the Tribunal to explain the income of the deceased but the same was not considered and 15% of future prospects only and sought for enhancement.

6. Learned counsel for the insurer of the Honda Activa has contended that the Tribunal erroneously attributed 50% contributory negligence against the owner of the Honda Activa in spite of proving complete negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus.
The driver of the KSRTC bus was prosecuted and the prosecution papers point out the negligence on his part.

Hence, the Insurer &
owner of the Honda Activa be exonerated from the liability and prays for a direction to the KSRTC to fully satisfy the award.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for the KSRTC contended that the material on record shows that the deceased was drawing salary of Rs.8,000/- per month.
Income Tax Returns filed by the petitioners have no relevance as no particulars is placed before the court.
The Tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.
It is not disputed that the age of the deceased is 28 years and future prospects should be taken only 40% as the deceased was working in a private institution.
The accident was due to collision between NC: 2024:KHC:32341 the Bike and Honda Activa, the Bus has no role in the accident.
Attribution of 50% negligence against the KSRTC bus is not proper.
It is further contended that no banks will offer interest at 8% p.a., the Tribunal, without recording any reason, awarded such interest ant it needs modification .

sentences.text: 5 9. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for both parties and perused the records.
10. The first point is regarding the contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing Registration No.KA-03-HF-9043.

It is the contention of the KSRTC that the NC:
2024:KHC:32341 accident took place due to negligent riding by the rider of the Honda Activa and the deceased himself.

It is forcefully argued by the learned counsel for the KSRTC that there are two motor cycles involved in the accident i.e, Honda Activa bearing Registration No.KA-03-HF-9043 driven by one Dr.Syed Tahseen Ahmed, who has filed the complaint to the police and the Motor Cycle bearing Registration No.KA-50-Q-6676 rode by the deceased.
The Tribunal, on the ground that the deceased was also negligent attributed equal negligence against him.
11. In this regard, it is relevant to refer to the complaint lodged by one Dr.Syed Tahseen Ahmed, who is the eye witness and rider cum owner of the Honda Activa.

The averments made in the complaint which is marked at Exhibit P.2 clearly shows that on 29.06.2013 at 10:30 A.M., while he was riding Honda Activa, the deceased was riding his bike beside him, near Allalasandra Railway Gate, a KSRTC bus bearing Registration No.KA-40-F-310, came from behind and dashed against the bike of the deceased.
12.
Exhibit P3, spot panchanama points out that the road is running towards Yelahanka, bike and Honda Activa going ahead of bus, KSRTC bus hit against the bike of the deceased.
The averments made in the charge sheet/Exhibit P.4, clearly points out that the KSRTC bus came behind the Bike and Honda Activa.
Both bike, Honda Activa and KSRTC bus have been subjected to the motor vehicle inspection.
The front bumper of the KSRTC bus was damaged.

Tail lamp, rear indicator, muffler, doom, front wheel mud guard of the Honda Activa was damaged and the tail lamp, rear left indicator, front bumper and front right foot rest, gear lever of the Bike of the deceased was damaged.
This indicates that the KSRTC bus had hit from behind the Bike of the deceased as well as Honda Activa.
13. Exhibit P6-Spot sketch points out that at the spot, width of the road is 30 Feet.
No explanation was offered why the KSRTC bus had hit against the Bike and Honda Activa.
Evidence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, which is available on record as RW.1, G.R.Anil Kumar.

His testimony points out that both the Honda Activa and motor cycle of the deceased were standing side by side at the road divider, they moved the vehicle in hurried manner and as a result they collided each other.
If his evidence is to be accepted, why the bumper of the KSRTC bus got damaged in - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32341 the accident remains unanswered.
There is no corresponding damage to bike and Honda Activa to say they collided side by side.

sentences.text: Neither the driver nor KSRTC have challenged the prosecution of the driver.
There is no evidence on record to explain it was an inter se accident between the bike of the deceased and Honda Activa.
The driver of the KSRTC bus has been negligent.
On careful perusal of the impugned judgment, the Tribunal did not discuss anything about the inter se accident between the motor cycle of the deceased and Honda Activa.
When the KSRTC bus had hit the bike of the deceased and Honda Activa, which were going adjacent to each other, it is not appropriate to attribute negligence against riders.
Hence, attribution of contrary negligence against the Honda Activa at 50% is uncalled for and the KSRTC has to shoulder entire responsibility.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the Insurer, the rider of the bike as well as the Insurer have to be exonerated.
15. The point now arises for consideration is quantum of compensation.
The Tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- added 15% of future prospects for the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:32341 age of 28 years.

The Tribunal placed reliance on Exhibit P.9, the offer letter of Dr.Agarwal's Health Care Ltd., where the petitioner was offered to work as an Executive-Marketing and he was offered salary of Rs.8,000/- per month in the year 2011.
The compensation awarded under the Conventional Head is not in compliance of settled principle of law laid down in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others 1.

sentences.text: As regarding income of the deceased, though Income Tax Returns are filed, there is no evidence that additional income is from the transport business maintained by the deceased.
When the deceased was working as full fledged employee at Dr.Agarwal's Health Care Ltd., though his employment is at the private institution, it cannot be said as temporary employment.

Confirmation and increment letter given to the deceased is also placed at Exhibit P.11 and Salary Certificate of the deceased is (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009)6 SCC 121 (2018)18 SCC 130 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:32341 produced at Exhibit P.21.
The gross salary of the deceased is Rs.10,500/-for the month of June, 2013.
Total deduction constitute Rs.1,054/- including Rs.150/- towards Professional Tax.
The Tribunal did not consider these aspects.
When the deceased was drawing salary of Rs.10,500/- in the month of accident, it is relevant document to consider the income of the deceased.
Hence, income of the deceased is taken at Rs.10,500/- as against Rs.8,000/-.
The deceased died at the age of 28.
Exhibits P.9 and 11 shows that he has future prospects of getting higher salary by putting more number of service.
Hence, the future prospects has to be awarded at 50% as against 15% taken by the Tribunal.
The accident is 11 years old.

In view of the Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd vs Smt Tintu Eldhose on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33142710/
7 principle laid down in Pranay Sethi (supra), 10% has to be given as appreciation for the compensation awarded under the Conventional Heads.
